vs_ollama_n20.interpretation: Claude lifts D1 (+0.10) via aggressive rubric floor but regresses D3 sharply (−0.40). Likely model behavior difference, not prompt regression: Claude generates more plausible SUPPORTED hypotheses on clean commits (6/10 false HIGH), inflating D1 while D3 judge scores generic/wrong mechanisms at 0. Ollama assigned all commits MEDIUM, masking rubric floor and yielding higher D3 on the subset where it happened to match.

vs_full_gate_n50.note: iter-1 interim targets met; full delivery gate requires n=50 confirmation

strata_analysis.pattern: Agent is aggressive — high buggy recall (8/10 HIGH) but poor clean precision (6/10 false HIGH). Rubric criteria (a)/(b) fire on plausible integration-risk narratives even on clean commits.

likely_causes: Claude SUPPORTED-hypothesis generation on clean commits produces confident but wrong mechanisms — judge scores 0 (e.g., b9f1653 Jetty comment removal, 24d9de042248 ehcache property rename)
90846b5 wrong root cause persists on Claude (binary incompatibility vs actual Spring Boot deadlock) — agent reasoning failure, not judge infra
f897d46 D3=0.0 on both n=5 and commit-smoke due to JIRA missing description — judge infra, not prompt
Same-model judge may inflate Ollama D3 when agent hedges with generic structure; Claude's assertive wrong hypotheses score 0 more consistently

tier_2_pivot.assessment: Improvement on both dimensions vs pre-iter baseline — tier-2 loop experiments NOT auto-triggered
Both ΔD1 (+0.20) and ΔD3 (+0.07) exceed pivot thresholds. Prompt-only iter-1 shows measurable lift on production model. D3 Ollama gap is a calibration finding, not a pivot trigger.

recommendation.rationale: iter-1 contract PASS on Claude interim targets. Before iter-2 n=50 validation, classify D3≤0.25 commits from Claude n=20 (and available Ollama runs) into {hedging, generic-structure, missing-context-likely, judge-infra, wrong-mechanism}. The −0.40 D3 Ollama-vs-Claude gap and 6/10 clean false-HIGH pattern need forensics to decide whether iter-2 is prompt tuning (clean-commit rubric guard, hedge calibration) or loop change (EXP-BUNDLE-EXPAND). EXP-FORENSICS-TAG is parallel-safe, ~$0.05, and directly informs iter-2 scope.
sequencing: 1. EXP-FORENSICS-TAG — tag D3 failures on Claude n=20 eval JSONs
2. EXP-JUDGE-SWAP — cross-model re-score n=20 before trusting D3=0.20 at boundary
3. iter-2 prep — if >40% missing-context-likely, prioritize EXP-BUNDLE-EXPAND; if wrong-mechanism/clean-FP dominant, prompt rubric amendment for clean commits
4. EXP-MULTITURN-AB — run after forensics; may help 90846b5-class integration defects
5. iter-2 n=50 — only after forensics + judge-swap clarify D3 signal
recommendation.do_not: Do not skip forensics and jump to iter-2 n=50 — D3 at exact boundary (0.20) with known Ollama divergence and clean FP rate warrants diagnosis first.
